items.title: Arturo O'Farrill interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2024
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Another Arturo — Sandoval — told me that he’s been typecast in the film world... And I wonder if the people that come to you for commissions, do they have that in their mind?

ctx.x: human being who is — you know who is so chained down. So even as I’m writing this ballet, with a fantastic ballet company and a fantastic symphony orchestra and a fantastic operatic setting, I found it incredibly freeing because I knew that with all these contractions, with all these straight jackets, that I was only going to be able to be myself. That was the only way I was going to be able to do it authentically. And so I did some of my most — I think I did some of my most honest composition in the midst of…

Another Arturo — Sandoval — told me that he’s been typecast in the film world, “Yes, call on him if you need something Latino.” And I wonder if the people that come to you for commissions, do they have that in their mind?

I think that the San Francisco Ballet commission did, but I think a lot of the work that I get as a composer is strictly because of them wanting my sound, them wanting my approach. I did a composition for the NPR local station WNYC. They commissioned me to write a piece and they put no such constraints on me. They just saw me as a modernist and that I could do whatever I want — they didn’t ask for Latin music. The point — here’s the thing about — I was trying to get out earlier. I don’t fit — I’m trans-culture.…
